items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: And you know we became friends.

ctx.x: I liked what you said about the theory coming after the creativity. Every once in a while I put on Cannonball’s, one of his very first records with Miles was on it, and they played “Autumn Leaves.” And the solo that Cannonball plays is utterly fascinating. And he’s got all these sort of not-in-the-chord tones, but the way he fashions them I’m just in awe.

You know you don’t hear Cannonball so much but I was very lucky — we went to hear Cannonball in Dallas when I was in North Texas and it was when I was first writing. And I wrote a chart called “Codify” which is an abstract sort of 13-bar blues. And we had a great band and Cannonball, I remember that he — of course I don’t remember anything melodically about what he played but I remember he played “Carnival” and he played like 13 choruses. And I had tears in my eyes at the end of it you know. And we went up and…

up. They came up to the school the following day. And so everybody was thrilled and Leon Breedon says, “This is a new chart by Lou Marini.” And we played the chart and when we finished it I looked up and everybody in the band was looking at me. And at first I was like what’s going on. And then I realized that Cannonball and Nat are standing right behind me over my shoulders, and Cannonball leans over to me and he says, “Lou, you a crazy motherfucker.” And you know we became friends. And I ran into him like with…
